subject: Clarifying where customer data is processed, retention, and deletion steps
messages:
From: Grace Li <grace.li@finserve.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: security@finserve.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Quick Qs on where FinServe data is processed / retention

Hi Dev,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team found the latency numbers helpful. Before we move to procurement, Security has a couple of clarifying questions about data residency and deletion for our compliance review: 

- Which geographic regions will our request/response data and embeddings be processed in when we use the hosted API?
- Do you use any subprocessors that have data centers outside the EU? If so, who and for what purpose?
- What are Redwood's default retention windows for transient request logs vs. customer-configured data? What is the process to request deletion of historic data?

Can you point me to any diagrams or a short one-pager we can share with Security?

Appreciate a concise summary — they like bullets.

Thanks,
Grace Li
Security & Privacy Lead
FinServe

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Li <grace.li@finserve.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where FinServe data is processed / retention

Hi Grace — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (infra/security engineer) and Hannah (compliance) to give the technical and policy details. I attached a short processing map and a retention schedule that should help share with your Security team.

High-level answers first (bulleted):
- Regions: Hosted API requests are served primarily from our EU region for EU customers by default (Ireland and Frankfurt deployments). We can pin to EU-only processing for enterprise accounts via a residency contract.
- Subprocessors: Core compute runs on our managed provider (RedCloud) in the regions above; we also use ObjectStoreCo for durable storage and LogStream for ephemeral request logs. Both have EU data center footprints; some support cross-border replication for resilience.
- Retention: Default transient logs (request traces, debugging buffers) are retained 30 days. Customer-configured artifacts (conversation histories retained for model context or embeddings) are retained per the customer's setting; default is 90 days. Deletion requests are handled via the Console or an API endpoint; we also support bulk deletion via signed request and an auditor flow.

Next steps: Karthik and Hannah, could you add any technical caveats on cross-border transfers and the deletion SLA? Grace — I included the two files referenced above.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-eu-processing-map.pdf (PDF, 420 KB)]
[Attachment: data-retention-schedule.csv (CSV, 4 KB)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Li <grace.li@finserve.com>, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where FinServe data is processed / retention

Hi Grace — adding the technical specifics you asked for (keeping bullets as requested):

1) Processing locations & routing
- Default behavior: For accounts flagged as EU-residency, API requests are routed to EU inference clusters (primary in eu-west-1 / Ireland; secondary eu-central-1 / Frankfurt for failover).
- Model artifacts (weights) are replicated to the EU clusters only for pinned models. For ephemeral hosted models we verify that runtime does not call services outside the EU by default.

2) Subprocessors (short list & purpose)
- RedCloud (compute orchestration) — EU data centers; used for GPU inference instances.
- ObjectStoreCo (durable object storage) — EU buckets used for customer blobs; cross-region replication optional (disabled by default for EU-residency accounts).
- LogStream (metrics & ephemeral logging) — collects traces; retention policy configurable; data-at-rest encrypted (AES-256).
- Telemetry vendors (error/uptime) — aggregated, PII-stripped telemetry may be sent to vendor endpoints in the EU. No raw customer request payloads are sent to third-party telemetry vendors.

3) Cross-border transfers & legal safeguards
- For EU customers who require no cross-border transfer, we offer contract terms that restrict processing to EU-only infrastructure and disable cross-region replication.
- Where transfers are necessary for support (e.g., a red-team debug session), we operate under Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and only after documented approvals.

4) Retention & deletion process
- Default retention: transient request logs = 30 days; customer-provisioned artifacts = 90 days.
- Deletion API: /v1/customers/{id}/data/delete (authenticated, returns job id). Typical deletion SLA: 7–30 days depending on the artifact type (index rebuilds and embedding stores can take longer due to background compaction).
- Audit trail: every deletion request generates an immutable audit record stored in our EU audit vault for 7 years (metadata only).

5) Evidence & attestation
- We can provide: SOC 2 Type II report excerpts, subprocessor roster with data center locations, and a short processing map PDF (attached). For regulated workloads we recommend a residency addendum (contract) and customer-controlled encryption keys (bring-your-own-key).

If you want, I can prepare a one-page diagram showing exactly which subprocessors touch raw request payloads.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Infra & Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where FinServe data is processed / retention

Grace — thanks for the quick turnaround on questions. To summarize and propose next steps for your Security review: 

Summary (short):
- EU-residency available by default for enterprise accounts: processing in Ireland + Frankfurt only; cross-border replication disabled by default.
- Subprocessors are EU-based for the services that touch request payloads; optional cross-region features exist but are off for residency customers.
- Retention: 30d transient logs, 90d default customer artifacts; deletion via API/Console with audit trail and 7–30 day SLA depending on artifact.
- Legal safeguards: SCCs for exceptional transfers; residency addendum + BYOK available for regulated accounts.

Proposed next steps:
1) I can share the SOC 2 excerpt and our subprocessor roster with your Security team — please confirm where to upload (Drive link / secure SFTP).
2) If you need an EU-only contract addendum, I can loop Legal and get a residency addendum draft to you in 3 business days.
3) Karthik can produce the one-page diagram of processing flow that highlights which subprocessors touch raw payloads.

If that works, let me know which of the three you want first and I'll get it moving.

Best,
Dev Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
